messages:
Clara: FYI from today's channel onramp call  cloud partner asked for clear wording on region price uplifts, hardware-lease vs appliance-purchase, and a clawback for extreme overconsumption. Need a short canonical thread we can copy into the PO attachment.
Jonah: Good ask. Let's be explicit: price uplift by region should be shown as a percent additive line on the waterfall, not baked into the list price. Makes reconciliation easier.
Mei: Also flag two hardware flows: lease (monthly line item) vs one-time purchase (capex). Lease counts as billable platform surcharge and does NOT count toward the commit. Purchase never counts toward commit unless partner explicitly includes it.
Oscar: On clawback: partner wants protection if customer massively overshoots committed units in month 1 (e.g., 3x). I propose a controlled overage tiering: up to 120% = normal overage pricing; 120-200% = elevated overage + notify and require capacity review; >200% = limited credit reversal clause (applies only to applied smoothing credits, not discounts).
Clara: Draft waterfall example (compact):
```
1) List price: $1,000/unit
2) Commit discount: -15% -> $850/unit
3) Region uplift (APAC): +8% -> $918/unit
4) Deployment surcharge (appliance lease): +5% -> $964/unit (lease billed monthly)
5) Vested smoothing credit applied after remediation election: up to $20k over 6mo
Net invoiced vs reserved credits displayed separately in billing PDF
```
Jonah: Add a clear line: "Which counts toward the commit?" Answer: units billed under the discounted platform line and reserved capacity SKUs count. Lease and one-time SI professional-services do NOT count unless explicitly enumerated.
Mei: Renewal guard: if trailing 3mo avg usage < 60% -> customer can elect (A) 3mo extension, or (B) apply up to 50% of remaining smoothing credits to next term. If trailing 3mo avg usage > 150% -> overconsumption review: elevated pricing band applies and RevOps will compute any retroactive credit adjustments (clawback applies only to smoothing credits that were applied earlier).
Oscar: Legal note: avoid the word "refund" anywhere. Use "adjustment" or "credit reversal". All adjustments require 30-day notice and a joint capacity review.
Clara: Marketplace SKU naming suggestion: "Redwood Commit (PrivOffer) - 1Y - Region:APAC" + attach a 1-pager that lists meter IDs and region uplift percent.
Jonah: Ops requirement: include meter parity tag + timezone tag so usage windows align with region billing. Reconciliation CSV delivered within 7 business days. Disputes within 45 days.
Mei: Finance nuance: appliance lease billed monthly recognized on delivery; smoothing credits are deferred. Clawback adjustments to smoothing credits reverse previously applied credits (accounting entry) but do not create a cash refund. We'll add a 1-line GAAP note in the attachment.
Oscar: Announcement timing: don't publish anything until partner confirms region uplift and appliance SKU images. Proposed cadence: partner announcement 10 days after close; marketplace private-offer live 21 days after close to allow AP setup for lease flows.
Clara: Partner stacking rule: default = no stacking with public promos. If partner requests stacking with co-marketing credits, those must be explicitly enumerated in the PO attachment and approved by RevOps.
Jonah: I'll draft a short contractual paragraph for overage tiers + clawback and share.
Mei: I'll draft the PO attachment template showing waterfall + meter IDs + GAAP note.
Oscar: I'll coordinate with Partner Marketing on messaging and partner-facing FAQ (include three short scenarios: underutilization, normal ramp, massive overconsumption).
partner-bot: Task created: region-uplift-and-clawback-playbook -> owner: Clara, due_in: 3 business days (task id: PO-4723).
Clara: Great work. Once drafts are in, we'll run Legal + RevOps for final wording. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
